paragraphs.sourceText: Tests may be the most unpopular part of academic life. Students hate them because they produce fear and 26 about being evaluated, and a focus on grades instead of learning for learning’s sake.

But tests are also valuable. A well-constructed test 27 what you know and what you still need to learn. Tests help you see how your performance 28 that of others. And knowing that you’ll be tested on 29 material is certainly likely to 30 you to learn the material more thoroughly.

However, there’s another reason you might dislike tests: You may assume that tests have the power to 31 your worth as a person. If you do badly on a test, you may be tempted to believe that you’ve received some 32 information about yourself from the professor, information that says you’re a failure in some significant way.

This is a dangerous—and wrong-headed —assumption. If you do badly on a test, it doesn’t mean you’re a bad person or stupid. Or that you’ll never do better again, and that your life is 33 If you don’t do well on a test, you’re the same person you were before you took the test—no better, no worse. You just did badly on a test. That’s it.
34 , tests are not a measure of your value as an individual—they are a measure only of how well and how much you studied. Tests are tools; they are indirect and 35 measures of what we know.

Municipal bonds, also secure, are offered by local governments and often have 36 such as tax-free interest. Some may even be 37 Corporate bonds are a bit more risky.

Two questions often 38 first-time corporate bond investors. The first is “If I purchase a corporate bond, do I have to hold it until the maturity date?,” The answer is no. Bonds are bought and sold daily on 39 securities exchanges. However, if you decide to sell your bond before its maturity date, you’re not guaranteed to get the face value of the bond. For example, if your bond does not have 40 that make it attractive to other investors, you may be forced to sell your bond at a 41 ,i.e., a price less than the bond’s face value. But if your bond is highly valued by other investors, you may be able to sell it at a premium, i.e., a price above its face value. Bond prices generally 42 inversely(相反地) with current market interest rates. As interest rates go up, bond prices fall, and versa（反之亦然）. Thus, like all investments, bonds have a degree of risk.

The second question is “ How can I 43 the investment risk of a particular bond issue? ”Standard & Poor’s and Moody’s Investors Service rate the level of risk of many corporate and government bonds. And 44 , the higher the market risk of a bond, the higher the interest rate. Investors will invest in a bond considered risky only if the 45 return is high enough.

Directions：In this section^ you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Lessons From a Feminist Paradise
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中^您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。女权主义天堂的教训

paragraphs.sourceText: A) On the surface, Sweden appears to be a feminist paradise. Look at any global survey of gender equality and Sweden will be near the top. Family-friendly policies are its norm—with 16 months of paid parental leave, special protections for part-time workers, and state-subsidized preschools where, according to a government website, “gender-awareness education is increasingly common.” Due to an unofficial quota system, women hold 45 percent of positions in the Swedish parliament. They have enjoyed the protection of government agencies with titles like the Ministry of Integration and Gender Equality and the Secretariat of Gender Research. So why are American women so far ahead of their Swedish counterparts in breaking through the glass ceiling?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 从表面上看，瑞典似乎是女权主义的天堂。看看任何关于性别平等的全球调查，瑞典都会名列前茅。家庭友好型政策已成为常态——16个月的带薪育儿假、对兼职工人的特殊保护以及国家补贴的幼儿园，据政府网站称，“性别意识教育越来越普遍”。由于非官方的配额制度，女性在瑞典议会中占有 45% 的职位。她们受到融合与性别平等部、性别研究秘书处等政府机构的保护。那么，为什么美国女性在突破玻璃天花板方面远远领先于瑞典女性呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) In a 2012 report, the World Economic Forum found that when it comes to closing the gender gap in “economic participation and opportunity,” the United States is ahead of not only Sweden but also Finland, Denmark, the Netherlands, Iceland, Germany, and the United Kingdom. Sweden’s rank in the report can largely be explained by its political quota system. Though the United States has fewer women in the workforce (68 percent compared to Sweden’s 77 percent), American women who choose to be employed are far more likely to work full-time and to hold high-level jobs as managers or professionals. They also own more businesses, launch more start-ups(新创办的企业）, and more often work in traditionally male fields. As for breaking through the glass ceiling in business, American women are well in the lead.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 世界经济论坛在2012年的一份报告中发现，在缩小“经济参与和机会”方面的性别差距方面，美国不仅领先于瑞典，还领先于芬兰、丹麦、荷兰、冰岛、德国和英国。瑞典在报告中的排名很大程度上可以通过其政治配额制度来解释。尽管美国劳动力中的女性人数较少（68%，而瑞典为 77%），但选择就业的美国女性更有可能从事全职工作，并担任经理或专业人士等高级职位。她们还拥有更多的企业，创办更多的初创企业，并且更多地在传统的男性领域工作。至于突破商业玻璃天花板，美国女性遥遥领先。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) What explains the American advantage? How can it be that societies like Sweden, where gender equality is vigorously pursued and enforced, have fewer female managers, executives, professionals, and business owners than the laissez-faire (自由放任的）United States? A new study by Cornell economists Francine Blau and Lawrence Kahn gives an explanation.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 什么解释了美国的优势？为什么像瑞典这样大力追求和执行性别平等的社会，女性经理、行政人员、专业人士和企业主的数量比自由放任的美国还要少呢？康奈尔大学经济学家弗朗辛·布劳和劳伦斯·卡恩的一项新研究给出了解释。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Generous parental leave policies and readily available part-time options have unintended consequences: instead of strengthening women’s attachment to the workplace, they appear to weaken it. In addition to a 16-month leave, a Swedish parent has the right to work six hours a day (for a reduced salary) until his or her child is eight years old. Mothers are far more likely than fathers to take advantage of this law. But extended leaves and part-time employment are known to be harmful to careers——for both genders. And with women a second factor comes into play: most seem to enjoy the flexible-time arrangement (once known as the “mommy track”) and never find their way back to full-time or high-level employment. In sum; generous family-friendly policies do keep more women in the labor market, but they also tend to diminish their careers.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 慷慨的育儿假政策和现成的兼职选择会带来意想不到的后果：它们非但没有加强女性对工作场所的依恋，反而削弱了这种依恋。除了 16 个月的假期外，瑞典父母还有权每天工作 6 小时（工资有所减少），直到他或她的孩子年满 8 岁。母亲比父亲更有可能利用这项法律。但众所周知，延长休假和兼职工作对男女职业生涯都有害。对于女性来说，第二个因素开始发挥作用：大多数人似乎喜欢灵活的时间安排（曾经被称为“妈妈轨道”），并且永远找不到回到全职或高水平工作的路。总而言之；慷慨的家庭友好政策确实让更多女性留在劳动力市场，但也往往会削弱她们的职业生涯。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) According to Blau and Kahn, Swedish-style paternal (父亲的）leave policies and flexible-time arrangements pose a second threat to women’s progress: they make employers cautious about hiring women for full-time positions at all. Offering a job to a man is the safer bet. He is far less likely to take a year of parental leave and then return on a reduced work schedule for the next eight years.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 根据布劳和卡恩的说法，瑞典式的父亲休假政策和灵活的工作时间安排对女性的进步构成了第二个威胁：它们让雇主在雇用女性担任全职职位时变得谨慎。为男性提供工作是更安全的选择。他不太可能休一年的育儿假，然后在接下来的八年里减少工作时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) I became aware of the trials of career-focused European women a few years ago when I met a postdoctoral student from Germany who was then a visiting fellow at Johns Hopkins. She was astonished by the professional possibilities afforded to young American women. Her best hope in Germany was a government job—prospects for women in the private sector were dim. “In Germany，” she told me, “we have all the benefits, but employers don’t want to hire us.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 几年前，当我遇到一位来自德国的博士后学生（当时是约翰·霍普金斯大学的访问学者）时，我开始意识到以职业为中心的欧洲女性所面临的考验。她对美国年轻女性所获得的职业机会感到惊讶。她在德国最大的希望是一份政府工作——私营部门的女性前景黯淡。 “在德国，”她告诉我，“我们拥有所有福利，但雇主不想雇用我们。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Swedish economists Magnus Henrekson and Mikael Stenkula addressed the following question in their 2009 study: why are there so few female top executives in the European egalitarian(平等主义的）welfare states? Their answer :“Broad-based welfare-state policies hinder women’s representation in elite competitive positions.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 瑞典经济学家 Magnus Henrekson 和 Mikael Stenkula 在 2009 年的研究中提出了以下问题：为什么欧洲平等主义福利国家的女性高管如此之少？他们的答案是：“基础广泛的福利国家政策阻碍了女性在精英竞争职位中的代表性。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) It is tempting to declare the Swedish policies regressive (退步的）and hail the American system as superior. But that would be shortsighted. The Swedes can certainly take a lesson from the United States and look for ways to clear a path for their ambitious female careerists. But most women are not committed careerists. When the Pew Research Center recently asked American parents to identify their “ideal” life arrangement, 47 percent of mothers said they would prefer to work part-time and 20 percent said they would prefer not to work at all. Fathers answered differently：75 percent preferred full-time work. Some version of the Swedish system might work well for a majority of American parents, but the United States is unlikely to fully embrace the Swedish model. Still, we can learn from their experience.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 人们很容易宣称瑞典的政策是倒退的（退步的），并称赞美国制度优越。但这将是短视的。瑞典人当然可以从美国吸取教训，并寻找方法为她们雄心勃勃的女性野心家扫清道路。但大多数女性都不是坚定的野心家。当皮尤研究中心最近要求美国父母确定她们的“理想”生活安排时，47％的母亲表示她们更愿意做兼职，20％的人表示她们更愿意父亲们的回答不同：75％的人更喜欢全职工作。瑞典的某些版本可能适合大多数美国父母，但美国不太可能完全接受瑞典模式。不过，我们可以学习他们的经验。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Despite its failure to shatter the glass ceiling, Sweden has one of the most powerful and innovative economies in the world. In its 2011-2012 survey, the World Economic Forum ranked Sweden as the world’s third most competitive economy; the United States came in fifth. Sweden, dubbed the “rockstar of the recovery” in the Washington Post. also leads the world in life satisfaction and happiness. It is a society well worth studying, and its efforts to conquer the gender gap impart a vital lesson—though not the lesson the Swedes had in mind.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 尽管未能打破玻璃天花板，瑞典仍然是世界上最强大和创新的经济体之一。在2011-2012年的调查中，世界经济论坛将瑞典列为世界第三大最具竞争力的经济体；美国排名第五。瑞典被《华盛顿邮报》称为“复苏的摇滚明星”。在生活满意度和幸福感方面也领先世界。这是一个非常值得研究的社会，它为克服性别差距所做的努力提供了重要的教训——尽管不是瑞典人想要的教训。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Sweden has gone farther than any other nation on earth to integrate the sexes and to offer women the same opportunities and freedoms as men. For decades, these descendants of the Vikings have been trying to show the world that the right mix of enlightened policy, consciousness raising, and non-sexist child rearing would close the gender divide once and for all. Yet the divide persists.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 瑞典在性别融合以及为女性提供与男性相同的机会和自由方面比地球上任何其他国家都走得更远。几十年来，这些维京人的后裔一直试图向世界表明，开明政策、提高意识和非性别歧视的儿童抚养方式的正确结合将一劳永逸地消除性别鸿沟。然而分歧仍然存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) A 2012 press release from Statistics Sweden bears the title “Gender Equality in Sweden Treading (踩) Water” and notes: • The total income from employment for all ages is lower for women than for men. • One in three employed women and one in ten employed men work part-time. • Women’s working time is influenced by the number and age of their children, but men’s working time is not affected by these factors. • Of all employees, only 13 percent of the women and 12 percent of the men have occupations with an even distribution of the sexes.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 瑞典统计局 2012 年的一份新闻稿标题为“踩水的瑞典性别平等”并指出： • 所有年龄段的就业总收入均低于男性。 • 三分之一的就业女性和十分之一的就业男性从事兼职工作。 • 女性的工作时间受子女数量和年龄的影响，但男性的工作时间不受这些因素的影响。 • 在所有员工中，只有 13% 的女性和 12% 的男性从事的职业性别分布均匀。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Confronted with such facts, some Swedish activists and legislators are demanding more extreme and far- reaching measures, such as replacing male and female pronouns with a neutral alternative and monitoring children more closely to correct them when they gravitate (被吸引) toward gendered play. When it came to light last year that mothers, far more than fathers, chose to stay home from work to care for their sick kids, Ulf Kristersson, minister of social security, quickly commissioned a study to determine the causes of and possible cures for this disturbing state of affairs.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 面对这些事实，一些瑞典活动家和立法者要求采取更极端和影响更深远的措施，例如用中性替代品取代男性和女性代词，并更密切地监控儿童，当他们倾向于性别游戏时予以纠正。去年，当人们发现更多的母亲选择不工作在家照顾生病的孩子时，社会保障部长乌尔夫·克里斯特森(Ulf Kristersson)迅速委托开展一项研究，以确定这种令人不安的状况的原因和可能的治疗方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Swedish family policies, by accommodating women’s preferences effectively, are reducing the number of women in elite competitive positions. The Swedes will find this paradoxical and try to find solutions. Let us hope these do not include banning gender pronouns, policing children’s play, implementing more gender quotas, or treating women5s special attachment to home and family as a social injustice. Most mothers do not aspire to (向往）elite, competitive full-time positions: the Swedish policies have given them the freedom and opportunity to live the lives they prefer. Americans should look past the gender rhetoric and consider what these Scandinavians have achieved. On their way to creating a feminist paradise, the Swedes have unintentionally created a haven (避风港）for normal mortals.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）瑞典的家庭政策通过有效地照顾女性的偏好，正在减少处于精英竞争职位的女性数量。瑞典人会发现这种矛盾并试图寻找解决方案。让我们希望这些措施不包括禁止性别代词、监管儿童游戏、实施更多性别配额，或将女性对家庭的特殊依恋视为社会不公正。大多数母亲并不渴望成为精英、有竞争力的全职职位：瑞典的政策给了她们自由和机会，让她们过上自己喜欢的生活。美国人应该超越性别言论，考虑这些斯堪的纳维亚人所取得的成就。在创造女权主义天堂的路上，瑞典人无意中为普通人创造了避风港。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Sweden has done more than other nations to close the gender gap, but it continues to exist.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 瑞典在缩小性别差距方面比其他国家做得更多，但这种差距仍然存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Sweden is one of the most competitive economies in the world and its people enjoy the greatest life satisfaction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 瑞典是世界上最具竞争力的经济体之一，其人民享有最高的生活满意度。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. More American women hold elite job positions in business than Swedish women.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 与瑞典女性相比，更多的美国女性在商界担任精英职位。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Swedish family-friendly policies tend to exert a negative influence on women’s careers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 瑞典的家庭友好政策往往对妇女的职业产生负面影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. The quota system in Sweden ensures women’s better representation in government.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 瑞典的配额制度确保妇女在政府中有更好的代表权。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Though the Swedish model appears workable for most American parents, it may not be accepted by them in its entirety.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 尽管瑞典模式对大多数美国父母来说似乎可行，但他们可能无法完全接受。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Swedish women are allowed the freedom and opportunity to choose their own way of life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 瑞典妇女有选择自己生活方式的自由和机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Texting has long been bemoaned (哀叹）as the downfall of the written word, “penmanship for illiterates,” as one critic called it. To which the proper response is LOL. Texting properly isn’t writing at all. It’s a “spoken” language that is getting richer and more complex by the year.
paragraphs.translationZh: 发短信长期以来一直被哀叹为书面文字的衰落，正如一位批评家所称，“文盲的书法”。对此正确的反应是哈哈。正确的发短信根本不是写作。它是一种“口语”语言，而且逐年变得更加丰富和复杂。

paragraphs.sourceText: First, some historical perspective. Writing was only invented 5 500 years ago, whereas language probably traces back at least 80 000 years. Thus talking came first; writing is just a craft that came along later. As such, the first writing was based on the way people talk, with short sentences. However, while talking is largely subconscious and rapid, writing is deliberate and slow. Over time, writers took advantage of this and started crafting long-winded sentences such as this one: “The whole engagement lasted above 12 hours, till the gradual retreat of the Persians was changed into a disorderly flight, of which the shameful example was given by the principal leaders and...”
paragraphs.translationZh: 首先，一些历史观点。文字的发明只有 5500 年前，而语言可能至少可以追溯到 80000 年前。因此，谈话是第一位的；写作只是后来出现的一门手艺。因此，最初的写作是基于人们说话的方式，用短句。然而，虽然说话很大程度上是潜意识的、快速的，但写作却是深思熟虑的、缓慢的。随着时间的推移，作家们利用这一点，开始写出这样的长句：“整个交战持续了12个小时以上，直到波斯人的逐渐撤退变成了无序的逃跑，其中可耻的例子是由主要领导人和……”

paragraphs.sourceText: No one talks like that casually—or should. But it is natural to desire to do so for special occasions. In the old days, we didn’t much write like talking because there was no mechanism to reproduce the speed of conversation. But texting and instant messaging do—and a revolution has begun. It involves the crude mechanics of writing, but in its economy, spontaneity and even vulgarity, texting is actually a new kind of talking, with its own kind of grammar and conventions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 没有人会这么随意地说话——也不应该这样。但在特殊场合希望这样做是很自然的。过去，我们不像说话那样写作，因为没有机制来重现谈话的速度。但短信和即时消息确实如此，一场革命已经开始。它涉及到原始的写作技巧，但就其经济性、自发性甚至粗俗而言，短信实际上是一种新的谈话方式，有自己的语法和惯例。

paragraphs.sourceText: Take LOL. It doesn’t actually mean “laughing out loud” in a literal sense anymore. LOL has evolved into something much subtler and sophisticated and is used even when nothing is remotely amusing. Jocelyn texts “Where have you been?” and Annabelle texts back “LOL at the library studying for two hours. ” LOL signals basic empathy(同感）between texters, easing tension and creating a sense of equality. Instead of having a literal meaning, it does something —conveying an attitude—just like the ending conveys past tense rather than “meaning” anything. LOL, of all things, is grammar.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈哈。它实际上不再是字面意义上的“大声笑”。 LOL 已经演变成一种更加微妙和复杂的东西，即使没有什么有趣的事情也会被使用。乔斯林发短信“你去哪儿了？”安娜贝尔回短信说“哈哈，在图书馆学习了两个小时。”哈哈标志着发短信者之间基本的同理心，缓解紧张并创造一种平等感。它没有字面意义，而是做了一些事情——传达一种态度——就像结尾传达过去时而不是“意思”任何东西。哈哈，最重要的是语法。

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course no one thinks about that consciously. But then most of communication operates without being noticed. Over time, the meaning of a word or an expression drifts —meat used to mean any kind of food, silly used to mean, believe it or not, blessed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，没有人有意识地思考这一点。但大多数的交流都是在不被注意的情况下进行的。随着时间的推移，一个词或一个表达方式的含义发生了变化——肉曾经意味着任何种类的食物，愚蠢过去意味着，不管你信不信，有福。

paragraphs.sourceText: Civilization, then, is fine—people banging away on their smartphones are fluently using a code separate from the one they use in actual writing, and there is no evidence that texting is ruining composition skills. Worldwide people speak differently from the way they write, and texting—quick, casual and only intended to be read once—is actually a way of talking with your fingers. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，文明是好的——人们在智能手机上敲击，流利地使用与他们在实际写作中使用的代码不同的代码，并且没有证据表明发短信会破坏写作技巧。世界各地的人们说话的方式与书写的方式不同，而发短信——快速、随意且只读一次——实际上是一种用手指说话的方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s possible to admire Oprah Winfrey and still wish Harvard hadn’t awarded her an honorary doctor of law degree and the commencement(毕业典礼)speaker spot at yesterday’s graduation. There’s no question Oprah’s achievements place her in the temple of American success stories. Talent, charm, and an exceptional work ethic have rarely hurled anyone as far as they have this former abused teenage mother from rural Mississippi who became one of the worlds most successful entertainment icons and the first African-American female billionaire.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你可能很欣赏奥普拉·温弗瑞，但仍然希望哈佛大学没有在昨天的毕业典礼上授予她荣誉法学博士学位和毕业典礼演讲嘉宾席位。毫无疑问，奥普拉的成就使她跻身美国成功故事的殿堂。这位来自密西西比州农村的前受虐待的少女母亲，后来成为世界上最成功的娱乐偶像之一，也是第一位非裔美国女性亿万富翁，才华、魅力和卓越的职业道德很少能将任何人抛到如此地步。

paragraphs.sourceText: Honorary degrees are often conferred on non-academic leaders in the arts, business, and politics. Harvard’s list in recent years has included Kofi Annan, Bill Gates, Meryl Streep, and David Souter. But Oprah’s particular brand of celebrity is not a good fit for the values of a university whose motto (座右铭）, Veritas, means truth. Oprah’s passionate advocacy extends, unfortunately, to a hearty embrace of fake science. Most notoriously, Oprah’s validation of Jenny McCarthy’s claim that vaccines cause autism (自闭症) has no doubt contributed to much harm through the foolish avoidance of vaccines.
paragraphs.translationZh: 荣誉学位通常授予艺术、商业和政治领域的非学术领袖。近年来哈佛大学的名单包括科菲·安南、比尔·盖茨、梅丽尔·斯特里普和大卫·苏特。但奥普拉独特的名人形象与大学的价值观不太相符，大学的座右铭是真理。不幸的是，奥普拉的热情倡导延伸到了对假科学的热心拥护。最臭名昭著的是，奥普拉证实了珍妮·麦卡锡关于疫苗导致自闭症的说法，无疑因愚蠢地回避疫苗而造成了很大的伤害。

paragraphs.sourceText: Famous people are entitled to a few failings, like the rest of us, and the choice of commencement speakers often reflects a balance of institutional priorities and aspirations. Judging from our conversations with many students, Oprah was a widely popular choice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与我们其他人一样，名人也有可能遭遇一些失败，而毕业典礼演讲者的选择往往反映了机构优先事项和愿望的平衡。从我们与许多学生的谈话来看，奥普拉是一个广泛受欢迎的选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: But this vote of confidence in Oprah sends a troubling message at precisely the time when American universities need to do more to advance the cause of reason. As former Dean of Harvard College, Harry Lewis，noted in a blog post about his objections, “It seems very odd for Harvard to honor such a high profile popularizer of the irrational... at a time when political and religious nonsense so jeopardize the rule of reason in this allegedly enlightened democracy and around the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但在美国大学需要采取更多行动来推进理性事业之际，这次对奥普拉的信任投票发出了一个令人不安的信息。正如哈佛大学前院长哈里·刘易斯（Harry Lewis）在一篇关于他的反对意见的博客文章中指出的那样，“在这个所谓的开明民主国家和世界各地，政治和宗教的胡言乱语如此危及理性统治的时候，哈佛大学却向如此高调的非理性普及者授予荣誉，这似乎很奇怪。

paragraphs.sourceText: As America’s oldest and most visible university, Harvard has a special opportunity to convey its respect for science not only through its research and teaching programs but also in its public affirmation of evidence-based inquiry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为美国历史最悠久、知名度最高的大学，哈佛大学拥有特殊的机会来表达其对科学的尊重，不仅通过其研究和教学项目，而且还通过其对循证探究的公开肯定。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, many American universities seem awfully busy protecting their brand name and not nearly busy enough protecting the pursuit of knowledge. A recent article in The Harvard Crimson noted the shocking growth of Harvard’s public relations arm in the last five years and it questioned whether a focus on risk management and avoiding controversy was really the best outward-looking face of this great institution.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，许多美国大学似乎非常忙于保护自己的品牌，而没有足够忙于保护对知识的追求。 《哈佛深红》最近发表的一篇文章指出，哈佛公共关系部门在过去五年中取得了令人震惊的增长，并质疑注重风险管理和避免争议是否真的是这个伟大机构最好的外向面孔。

paragraphs.sourceText: As American research universities begin to resemble profit centers and entertainment complexes, it’s easy to lose sight of their primary mission：to produce and spread knowledge. This mission depends on traditions of rational discourse and vigorous defense of the scientific method. Oprah Winfrey’s honorary doctorate was a step in the wrong direction. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着美国研究型大学开始类似于利润中心和娱乐中心，人们很容易忽视它们的主要使命：生产和传播知识。这一使命取决于理性话语的传统和对科学方法的大力捍卫。奥普拉·温弗瑞的荣誉博士学位是朝着错误方向迈出的一步。
